custom_logic_notes: The EA implements Burg's maximum entropy method (MEM) for spectral analysis and linear prediction. The core algorithm: (1) Detrends input price series, (2) Computes reflection coefficients via Burg's method minimizing forward/backward prediction errors, (3) Solves AR coefficients via Levinson-Durbin recursion, (4) Extrapolates price series forward by 'ForecastBars' bars using the AR model, (5) Generates buy signal when extrapolated curve trends above current close, sell when below. No SL/TP by default - exits only on signal reversal. The forecast is recomputed each new bar. Degree parameter controls AR model order (complexity), ForecastBars controls how far ahead to extrapolate. Higher degree = more complex spectral model capturing more frequency components but risk of overfitting.
python_conversion_notes: The Burg/MEM algorithm must be ported from scratch - no direct library equivalent in standard Python trading frameworks. Use numpy for Levinson-Durbin recursion. scipy.signal has linear_prediction_coefficients but Burg-specific variant needs custom implementation. Key steps: (1) Implement Burg reflection coefficient computation with forward/backward error minimization, (2) Implement Levinson-Durbin recursion for AR coefficient extraction, (3) Implement AR forecast extrapolation, (4) Wrap as signal generator. The forecast curve visualization is not needed for trading - only the forecast direction relative to current price matters. Consider using statsmodels.tsa.ar_model.AutoReg as approximate alternative but Burg method has specific regularization properties that differ from Yule-Walker.
